turns: Proposal: The City of Flint, Michigan will switch its drinking water source from Detroit's treated supply to the Flint River for about two years to save money while a new pipeline is built. The existing city treatment plant will treat the river water. No corrosion control treatment is planned. The city has old lead service lines. The water plant supervisor says the plant is not ready. Decision makers: city emergency manager and the state environmental regulator. Switch date: April 2014. Educational exercise: apply the Ontario framework as if this project were proposed in Ontario. Disciplines: civil/environmental (water treatment) and mechanical (pipes, pumps, corrosion). Phase: pre-implementation, about to switch. Objective: save money on water for about 2 years until the new pipeline is ready. Scope: source switch, river-water treatment at the existing plant, distribution through the existing pipe network. Stakeholders: about 100,000 residents, many low-income, plus plant workers. No public consultation was held and residents were not told about the risks.
